rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Full sequential read, chunk by chunk. Two judgment calls held: (a) chunk 1 L9 'Once it mattered for this lecture: the draft had drifted from what I'd actually told it to write' is a forward-pointing teaser (unpacked later at chunk 2 L19 'The end-state that was not' and L27 'The frame I did not cite') — but L11 in the same chunk explicitly licenses this shape ('Those numbers are the story. Everything that follows is commentary.'), and 'this lecture'/'it'=Claude are both named earlier in the same chunk, so it reads as a self-announced tally-then-detail structure, not an unresolved referent. (b) chunk 5 L49 'You have just diagnosed gaps in the M5 packaged session and mapped the work you repeat across your stack' invokes two earlier module beats (exercises spot-gaps-build-the-loop and read-your-stack) that are not immediately adjacent in the module's deck order (per spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md L106: ...exercise read-your-stack → the-handoff-prompt → story-of-module-6...) — checked placement against the module include order per the carve-out instruction; this file functions as a closing memoir naming the module's own arc, which the carve-out's 'closers' language and rule 2's whole-deck-summing-closer precedent both cover. All other pronouns/demonstratives (it, that, them, those, this) resolve to an antecedent in the same sentence or same paragraph within the same chunk (e.g. L9 'It caught two more leaks' = the verifier loop named two clauses earlier; L15 'those three modules'/'It' = 'three modules'/'The agent' one clause earlier; L17 'it'/'them'/'the same word' = 'a word... hard-banned' named at the top of the same paragraph). Arc-earned terms (M5, the loop, chat-shaped, the reference artefact, the rules file) are established within the same file at or before first callback, per the carve-out.

One candidate: chunk 2 L23 'The closing lecture ended with a three-phrase benediction: "You know how to test. You know how to learn. You know how to encode."' names another file by its role (closing lecture) rather than its title, but unpacks the specific claim/quote in the same sentence, matching the rule's own PASS example ('the opening lecture's infinite chameleon: the LLM that flatters you...'). No other cross-file reference in the body; module-name callbacks (M5) are arc-earned per rule 1, not rule-2 positional pointers.

Every chunk (0-5) carries a multi-sentence, self-standing claim or narrative unit; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Chunk 0 (lines 1-6) alone carries the frame-setting premise ('I am going to tell you how this module got made... Then I am going to ask you to hold something uncomfortable about LLMs').

All five ## headers are true summaries of their chunk content under the sequential read: 'The numbers' -> a numeric tally (L9); 'Things that went sideways' -> seven failure-mode paragraphs; 'The generalisation' -> the three short claims plus the taste-closes-the-gap line; 'Then I compounded the session' -> the prompts-run-on-the-generation + rules-moved-into-skills action; 'What the loop is for' -> the loop's rationale and the student's job. No chunk's content contradicts its own header.

Self-grading superlative: none in body (grep for 'one of the most/the best/nothing else/unmatched' returns zero body hits; the maintainer's backing block itself records the closing superlative 'Nothing else does.' as already cut 2026-08-30). Not-X-not-Y-Z construction: none found. Number+retraction: none (all counts in chunk 1, e.g. 'Twenty-odd', 'Ten fixes applied in all', are stated flatly, never hedged-then-restated). Abstraction-noun stacks: none found; 'chat-shaped'/'un-packaged shape'/'the flattering end-state' are concrete, either arc-earned spine terms or immediately unpacked by the surrounding quotes. Verb triplets with an empty leg: none (Claude 'typed... recommended... came out chat-shaped' at L37 is three distinct, concretely elaborated actions, not a terse empty-verb triplet). Closest calls on anaphora/epistrophe, both held as PASS because the third leg adds new content: chunk 3 L51 'The loop exists because LLMs drift. The loop exists because rules leak. The loop exists because every session surprises you, even when the task looked the same' — third leg adds the task-similarity nuance, not filler; chunk 3 L37 'The loop caught what the subagents missed. I caught what the loop missed. You will catch what I missed' — third leg shifts tense/addressee to the reader, the didactic point of the piece; chunk 5 L55 echoes the same template with a new entity (a senior-persona sim) in the third leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, so headings should be claims. 'The numbers' (chunk 1) is explicitly named as an accepted catalogue heading by the rule text itself; 'Things that went sideways' (chunk 2) is the same catalogue shape (a list of seven distinct anecdotes); 'Then I compounded the session' (chunk 4) is a phase/section label inside a first-person narrative walk, also carved out; 'What the loop is for' (chunk 5) is claim-adjacent (a stated purpose the content then argues). 'The generalisation' (chunk 3, L29) is different in kind: it introduces a single consolidated law/thesis, not a catalogue of items, and per the rule's own binding clause ('the claim requirement binds law and consolidation slides — where the header IS the teaching and a label would waste the beat') this is exactly that slide — the section delivers the memoir's central claim (non-determinism; 'a rule in context is not a rule in the output') but the header only announces that a generalization is coming, rather than stating it. Harm: mild, not comprehension-blocking (the three short declaratives right under the header still land the claim on the same chunk, and TOC/nav-rail scanning is the only thing that loses the payload), which is why this is filed non-blocking per this rule's own convention (previously fired non-blocking on ten other lectures, never blocking).
